newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Lindt says 1996 sales up 5.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Lindt says 1996 sales up 5.8 pct.

text.p: Chocolate and confectionery maker Lindt & Spruengli AG said 1996 consolidated sales rose 5.8 percent to 973 million Swiss francs from 920 million the previous year.
"The weakening of the Swiss franc had, for the first time in three years, a positive impact," Lindt said in a statement that did not elaborate.
Lindt said net trade sales rose 3.8 percent in local currency.
Lindt said sales in Germany and Switzerland, two of its three biggest markets, did not quite reach 1995 levels due to a difficult economic environment and consumer behaviour.
"All other markets registered a significant increase in sales," it added.
It said new products and product concepts were largely responsible for growth.
Lindt said that detailed financial information would be given at an annual news conference on April 1.
